To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of chlordecone and carbon tetrachlorene is lethal in 3-month old Fischer 344 rats, but is tolerated without mortality by 24-month old Fischer 343 rats.
the CD+CCL4 combination causes 100% mortality of 3-month-old male F344 rats by 72h but none of the 24-month-old male F44 rats die.
middle-aged and old-aged Fischer 344 rats are resistant against chlordecone (CD) +CCl4 combination toxicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of age-related differences in liver injury and liver tissue repair in the F344 rat.
the effects of aging on the susceptibility of the Fischer 344 rat against the toxic effects of the pesticide chlordecone and its synergistic effects on CCl4 toxicity.
the effects of aging and chlordecone (CD) on the toxicity and tissue repair of carbon tetrachlride (CCl4).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD+CC14 combination in the F344 rats is age dependent.
the CD+CC4 combination causes a lethal liver injury only in the 3 month old rats, but the middle aged and old aged rats tolerate it well.
the CD+CC14 combination is more toxic in 3-month than in the middle-aged (14-month) and old-aged (24-month) male Fischer 334 rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aged F344 rats tolerate chlordecone-amplied CCl4 toxicity by early onset and robust tissue repair.
aged rats are more tolerant than adult rats against the CD+CC14 combination.
aged rats are tolerant to the hepatotoxic effects of the CD+Cl4 combination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aged rats are not necessarily less tolerant to hepatotoxic chemicals.
aged rats are not only resistant to liver injury but are also protected from the lethal effect by the CD+CCI4 combination.
the aged F344 rats are tolerant against CCl4 toxicity and this is due to a robust compensatory liver tissue repair response.
